hook: Decode a German letter about a parking fine: what you are accused of, what you must do by when, and what happens if you stay silent.
intro: An Anhörungsbogen – the letter a German Bußgeldstelle sends before it decides on a fine – of about 400 words, complete with letterhead, file reference and enclosures. It contains the legal basis („gemäß § 55 des Gesetzes über Ordnungswidrigkeiten (OWiG)“), the allegation as one long zu-infinitive („Ihnen wird zur Last gelegt, … geparkt zu haben, wodurch ein Einsatzfahrzeug der Feuerwehr behindert wurde“), the sanction (a Geldbuße – never a Geldstrafe – plus fees and one point), the rights and duties of the person concerned, the Äußerungsfrist („binnen einer Woche ab Zugang dieses Schreibens“), the reservation clauses (unbeschadet dessen, vorbehaltlich), the keeper’s liability for costs (§ 25a StVG), a remedies formula for a later Bescheid and the Anlagen. Read it with three questions: what is alleged, what must I do by when, and what happens otherwise.
tips[0].title: Anhörung ≠ Bescheid
tips[0].text: An Anhörung gives you the chance to respond before a decision; a Bescheid is the decision, and only a Bescheid can be challenged by Einspruch. The letter says so twice. The objection deadline (two weeks after service of a Bescheid) is not the response deadline (one week after receipt of this letter).
tips[0].trap: etwaig = “any, possible”: einen etwaigen Bußgeldbescheid is a notice that may or may not come – it has not been issued yet.
tips[0].check.why: An Anhörung only invites you to respond; Einspruch is possible against the decision itself, the Bescheid.
tips[0].visual.marks[0].label: you may reply
tips[0].visual.marks[1].label: the decision
tips[0].visual.marks[2].label: final
tips[1].title: Unpack the reservation clauses
tips[1].text: Officialese states a right and its limit in one breath. unbeschadet dessen = notwithstanding this / even so; vorbehaltlich Ihrer Angaben = subject to what you say, i.e. unless your statement changes things; nach Aktenlage = on the basis of the file as it stands.
tips[1].trap: freiwillig does not mean “without consequence”. Read both halves of the sentence.
tips[1].check.why: unbeschadet dessen limits what was just said: even so, the duty to pay remains.
tips[2].title: Rights and duties of the Betroffene
tips[2].text: Silence on the matter is allowed, personal details are compulsory, naming the driver is requested but not required for close relatives, and a lawyer is optional. If the driver cannot be identified in a parking case, the keeper pays the costs of the proceedings – not the fine.
tips[2].check.why: Personal details are compulsory; a statement on the matter, naming a close relative and a lawyer are all optional.
tips[3].title: Geldbuße, not Geldstrafe
tips[3].text: Ordnungswidrigkeit → Bußgeldverfahren → Geldbuße → Bußgeldbescheid. Straftat → Strafverfahren → Geldstrafe → Strafbefehl/Urteil. The letter stays entirely on the first track; zuzüglich adds fees on top of the fine.
tips[3].check.why: An Ordnungswidrigkeit leads to a Geldbuße; a Geldstrafe belongs to criminal proceedings for a Straftat.
table.caption: Formulae in the letter and what they mean
remember[0]: Anhörung (chance to respond, 1 week) vs Bescheid (decision, Einspruch within 2 weeks).
remember[2]: unbeschadet dessen = notwithstanding this; vorbehaltlich = subject to; etwaig = possible; zuzüglich = plus.
remember[3]: Halterhaftung (§ 25a StVG) covers the costs of the proceedings, not the fine or the point.
exam: Official letters like this appear in C2 exam reading — and, more urgently, in your own letterbox, where a missed deadline costs money.
